tip.palette.label: What is a palette?
tip.palette.p1: Picks which physical bead brand the pattern is matched to. After export, buy beads by the BOM from that brand.
tip.palette.p2: <accent>Manyou</accent> (漫游酱) · Chinese market, codes M01–M30 (v1 starter).
tip.palette.note: Bead codes are not interchangeable across brands.
tip.colorCap.label: What is color cap?
tip.colorCap.p1: Caps how many distinct colors the final pattern can use.
tip.colorCap.p2: <accent>Lower</accent> · Simpler look, fewer bead packs to buy. Detail collapses; good for shareable patterns.
tip.colorCap.p3: <accent>Higher</accent> · Closer to source, but you may end up buying a whole pack of a color you only use twice.
tip.colorCap.note: The algorithm keeps the top-N most-used colors and remaps the rest to the nearest kept color.
tip.dither.label: What is dithering?
tip.dither.p1: Dithering decides how to fake colors the palette doesn’t have exactly.
tip.dither.p2: <accent>None</accent> · Nearest-color match. Cleanest for cartoons, line art, pixel art.
tip.dither.p3: <accent>F-S</accent> · Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion. Use for photos and gradients — smoother transitions.
export.label: EXPORT
export.note: PNG for sharing on screen. The PDF prints at real size (1 cell = 5 mm) across A4 pages, with coordinates and a bead list.
